title: Normalized Engineering Findings Response v1
description: The response contract every candidate model must satisfy. Claims are EMITTED here as structured entities and relations rather than extracted post hoc from prose, because post-hoc extraction is an unmeasured LLM step applied asymmetrically across candidates. Every current model in the roster supports native structured output, so this costs nothing in fairness terms.

findings.description: Every issue found. Report coverage, not a filtered shortlist — filtering is a downstream scoring decision. An empty array is a valid answer and is scored as such.

abstentions.description: Questions the corpus does not support answering. Correct abstention earns full credit; guessing on an unanswerable item is penalized more than a normal false positive.

answers.description: Direct answers for suites that pose questions rather than ask for findings (the semantic suite). Each answer carries its own claim set so it can be graph-verified.

coverage_notes.description: What was examined and what was not. Used to distinguish 'looked and found nothing' from 'did not look'.

confidence.description: Calibrated probability that this claim is correct. Scored with a proper scoring rule (Brier, ECE) as its own axis — it is NOT blended into the quality index, because a slightly less accurate but well-calibrated model is often the better production choice.

ref.description: Name of the entity. A fully-qualified name resolves most reliably, but the resolver accepts simple names and disambiguates using the finding's evidence. Unresolvable refs are bucketed as UNRESOLVED and reported separately from wrong — see references/scoring-spec.md § Entity Resolution.

role.description: How this entity participates in the finding.

relation.description: A checkable assertion about the system. These are what the code graph verifies. Predicates outside the enum are accepted but graded as UNKNOWN rather than counted against the model.

negated.description: Assert the ABSENCE of a relation (e.g. no timeout configured). Verified the same way; absence claims are frequently the whole point of a resiliency finding.

evidence.description: Where in the corpus the claim can be checked. Evidence grounding is 25% of the quality index because the code graph makes it objective.

type.description: The specific finding type. Use a CWE identifier for security findings (e.g. CWE-89) and a controlled architecture/resiliency type otherwise (e.g. layer_violation, missing_timeout, unbounded_retry, shared_datastore, cyclic_dependency, single_az_dependency, shared_thread_pool). Matching against oracles tolerates one level of ontology distance.

status.description: SUSPECTED signals a finding worth surfacing that the model could not confirm from the corpus. It is scored with reduced precision cost — surfacing an honest suspicion should not be punished as hard as a confident false positive.

root_cause.description: WHY this is wrong, not what it is. Causal agreement with the oracle is required for full match credit.

exploitability.description: Security suite only. Distinguishes a demonstrable path from a pattern match.

compliance_status.description: Controls suite only. INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE is a first-class correct answer, not a failure to answer.
